The conversation explores the symbiotic relationship between both countries, with a particular focus on the creative industry as a powerful driver of economic development. A conversation about culture, creativity, international opportunities, investment, and the future of Nigeria’s creative economy.

videos.title: The Reality Of My Music Borders Around Love, Pain, Heartbreak And Clubbing To Cope: CKAY Reveals
videos.headline: The Reality Of My Music Borders Around Love, Pain, Heartbreak And Clubbing To Cope: CKAY Reveals
videos.description:
The artist stops by the studio to break down his latest album, sharing how his 2026 project tells a deeply personal story of heartbreak, healing, and moving forward. He reflects on his journey from the opening breakup track NDA to falling in love again on Eclair, taking full accountability for his past relationship while explaining how Lagos mainland dance music inspired him to push past standard Amapiano sounds.

Throughout the conversation, he discusses using club culture as a therapeutic space to transform pain into strength rather than running from it. He also details his current tour following a kickoff show in the Czech Republic, his upcoming stop in Marseille, France, and his commitment to closing out the run with a massive homecoming concert in Lagos. Finally, the emo Afrobeats artist shares his thoughts on international fan culture, emphasizing that local fans built Afrobeats, while opening up about how his gothic style and painted black nails serve as authentic self-expression.

videos.title: “Burna Boy Is a Huge Inspiration to My Sound” — Buff Opens Up on His Music, 10 Minutes & More
videos.headline: “Burna Boy Is a Huge Inspiration to My Sound” — Buff Opens Up on His Music, 10 Minutes & More
videos.description:
In this exclusive full interview on the Midday Show with Kemi Smalls and Brownish on 96.9 Cool FM, Nigerian artist 6uff (Buff / 6uffzaddy) opens up about his music journey, gym lifestyle, personality, and more.

From church drummer and producer (as Logic) to breakthrough artist, 6uff shares how he started making music in 2021 with “Selfish,” the story behind his stage name, and the impact of family support — especially his mom’s prayers.

He talks about his breakout tracks **Prodigy** and **Idi Amin**, the massive collaboration **10 Minutes** with Odumodublvck, **Ripper’s Fate** with Tuff King, his heavy bass signature sound, perfectionism in the studio, and upcoming projects (including possible links with Burna Boy and Rondtown).

Also covered:

- His 6’5” height and gym dedication (started with homemade cement weights)
- Ambivert personality vs high-energy stage presence and shirtless performances
- Football background (defensive midfield, Barcelona fan)
- Fitness advice, real-life song themes (betrayal, survival, hustle)
- Guilty pleasures, movie preferences, and dream Nigerian cypher line-up

Stream 6uff’s music:  
• 10 Minutes (with Odumodublvck)  
• Prodigy  
• Ripper’s Fate (with Tuff King)  
• And more

videos.title: How Ladipoe Became One of Nigeria's Best Rappers
videos.headline: How Ladipoe Became One of Nigeria's Best Rappers
videos.description:
​@LadipoeLOTR  studied Biology and Chemistry at the University of North Carolina before moving back home to Nigeria, hoping to make the big break as a Recording Artist. 

He was in luck. His mother found a kindred spirit: another rapper’s mother while taking a course at the Lagos Business School. That rapper was Wale “Tec” Davies of @showdemcamp. Tec felt his bars and invited him into a creative circle, which incubated acts like Show Dem Camp, Funbi, @temidollfacevevo4701, @temsbaby, and more. 

Poe announced his presence on “Feel Alright”- a collab with SDC and @Bojdrb, which has been credited as being a precursor to the iconic Palm Wine Music series. 

Don Jazzy's @MavinRecords  came calling, and Poe vowed to make the best of the opportunity. Nearly 10 years later, he’s found the type of mainstream appeal that once seemed out of reach. This year, he released "Revival", one of the year’s best releases, highlighting why he’s one of the country’s most beloved artists.  

On this episode of Overnight Success, he takes us on the long journey from medical professional to one of the country's premier rappers.

videos.title: "I Am In Love With My Music" - Fola On School, Life, and Afrobeats
videos.headline: "I Am In Love With My Music" - Fola On School, Life, and Afrobeats
videos.description:
Fola opens up about his journey, his creative process, and how he manages to balance it all. The rising star discusses the reality of juggling his university studies with his music career. He admits that while he is working on his final year project about classroom management, he sometimes has to skip class to focus on his craft. As an Economics student, he jokes that his books do not always balance and confuse him, but his music is his main business right now.

When discussing his sound, Fola reveals that his style is deeply influenced by the artists he grew up listening to, giving massive shoutouts to legends like Wande Coal, D'banj, Wizkid, and Davido. Even though he creates music with a romantic vibe, he insists he is not a big lover boy and is simply in love with his music.

Fola also shares the story behind his latest collaboration featuring Ayra Starr. Having already worked together on "Tornado", he knew she was the perfect fit and revealed that she sent her verse back almost immediately without any stress. Looking to the future, Fola mentions his upcoming US tour in two months and his strong desire to learn music production. As he perfectly puts it: he is not where he used to be, he is not where he wants to be, but it is only up from here.

videos.headline: Everlast on “Jump Around,” House of Pain, Eminem & Starting Over (Audio Only) | The Almanac of Rap
videos.description:
On this episode of The Almanac of Rap, Donwill sits down with multi-platinum, Grammy Award-winning artist Everlast for a wide-ranging conversation about reinvention, longevity and a career that has consistently refused to stay inside one genre.

Everlast reflects on returning to music with Embers to Ashes (https://everlast.ffm.to/emberstoashes) after nearly eight years, an album shaped by the pandemic, divorce, losing his home in the Woolsey Fire and eventually finding his way back to songwriting. He takes Don through his early days with Ice-T’s Rhyme Syndicate and Divine Styler, the friendships that connected him with DJ Muggs, B-Real and Cypress Hill, and the unlikely series of events that led to House of Pain and the creation of “Jump Around.”

The conversation also revisits the genre-smashing Judgment Night soundtrack, the transformation that produced Whitey Ford Sings the Blues and “What It’s Like,” his relationship with Yelawolf, and why his decades-old beef with Eminem is firmly in the past. Everlast also considers what it takes to create a genuine anthem in today’s algorithm-driven music industry and gives flowers to the artists who helped make his career possible. Everlast breaks down:

-Returning with Embers to Ashes after an eight-year album hiatus
-Losing his home in the Woolsey Fire and rebuilding his life
-How COVID and fatherhood changed his relationship with touring
-House of Pain's unexpected relationship with Ireland
-Everlast says his Eminem beef is long over.
